To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The new DAA drugs are effective and safe in the treatment of chronic HCV genotype 1, 2 or 3 infection; (2) The new DDA drugs are effective and well tolerated in patients with HCV genotype 2 or 5 infection and cirrhosis; and (3) The new DAD drugs are effective and tolerated in HCV genotype 3 infected patients with cirrhosis.

The prevalence of chronic HCV infection is 0.7% in the population of the state of Santa Catarina (SC), Brazil; 80% of HCV-infected patients are unaware of their infection; the most prevalent genotype is 3a, and the most frequent route of infection is intravenous drug use; 80% patients are eligible for treatment, and 50% of them are eligible for treatment with DAAs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of drugs for the treatment of chronic HCV infection, the so called direct acting antiviral agents (DAA).
the treatment of chronic HCV infection with the new DAAs, in a real world experience in Southern Brazil.

the development of new, efficient and environmentally friendly methods for the production of bioactive molecules, such as antibiotics, antitumoral agents, anti-inflammatory and antivirals, from renewable sources.
